definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese low table with an electric heater underneath and a blanket that drapes over the sides to trap heat, used for warming the lower body during cold weather.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{炬燵|こたつ}に{入|はい}ってみかんを{食|た}べるのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: In winter, I like getting into the kotatsu and eating mandarin oranges.

examples.japanese: {炬燵|こたつ}から{出|で}たくない。
examples.english: I don't want to get out of the kotatsu.

examples.japanese: {炬燵|こたつ}で{寝|ね}ると{風邪|かぜ}をひくよ。
examples.english: You'll catch a cold if you fall asleep in the kotatsu.

notes:
The {炬燵|こたつ} is a quintessential Japanese winter comfort item. It consists of a low wooden table frame covered with a futon or heavy blanket, with a heat source underneath. Modern kotatsu typically use electric heaters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炬燵|こたつ}に{入|はい}る (to get into the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}から{出|で}る (to get out of the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}を{出|だ}す (to set up the kotatsu)
- {炬燵|こたつ}を{しまう|しまう} (to put away the kotatsu)

CULTURAL NOTES:
- Traditionally associated with eating みかん (mandarin oranges) while staying warm in winter.
- The combination of {炬燵|こたつ}とみかん is a stereotypical image of Japanese winter comfort.
- Sleeping in the {炬燵|こたつ} is considered unhealthy as only the lower body stays warm.
